meta.description: Register, clock and evidence trail for GDPR Articles 15 to 22.

props.title: Data subject requests
props.subtitle: One month from the day it arrived (Art. 12(3)). Sorted by the day you run out of time.

props.title: How the clock works here
props.text: The due date is stored on each request, not calculated when you look at it. Logging a request sets it to the day it arrived plus 30 days — never later than the statutory month. Taking an extension adds two months and records the reason and the day you told the requester, which is what makes the extension lawful. The due date stays editable in the grid, so you can set the exact calendar date.

props.emptyText: Nothing is due in the next week. That is the goal.
No requests yet. Log the first one.

screens.name: Log a request
screens.description: Register a request the day it arrives.

props.title: Log a request
props.subtitle: Six fields and a date. Everything else can be filled in on the case file.

props.title: Received, not noticed
props.text: Use the day the request ARRIVED, including one that came in by phone or reached the wrong inbox first. The month runs from then, and the due date is set from it. A request does not have to cite an Article, or the word "GDPR", to be one.

props.name: newrequest
props.submitLabel: Log it and start the clock

props.name: identifiers
props.label: Identifiers to search on
props.placeholder: Account name, customer number, old e-mail address, order references…

props.name: summary
props.label: What exactly was asked
props.placeholder: In the requester’s own words where possible.

screens.name: Case file
screens.description: One request: identity, searches, what was sent, what was withheld.

props.title: Do not disclose anything yet
props.text: This requester has not been verified. Answering the wrong person is itself a personal data breach. Record the check on the Identity tab — and if identity cannot be established, refuse under Art. 12(6) and record that as the ground, rather than letting the request go quiet.

props.emptyText: Open a request from the register.
No identity check recorded — nothing may be disclosed until there is one. Open a request from the register first.

options.label: Signed in to the known account
Reply to the address already on file

props.name: notes
props.label: What was seen, and what was not kept
props.placeholder: Data minimisation: say what you looked at, and confirm the copy was destroyed.

props.title: Searching the knowledge bases
props.text: The button below searches this workspace’s knowledge bases for the identifiers on this request and writes what came back straight into the log — dated, attributed and marked as automated. It does nothing until an editor picks the knowledge bases in App Studio (open this app, select the "Search the knowledge bases" action, add them to its knowledge base list). Everything else works without it: log each system you searched by hand. The log is the evidence either way.

props.emptyText: Nothing searched yet. A request answered without a search log cannot be shown to have been answered properly.

props.name: findings
props.label: What was found (or that nothing was)
props.placeholder: "Nothing" is a finding, and worth recording.

props.name: contents
props.label: What exactly was sent
props.placeholder: The categories of data, the files, the covering letter.

props.title: Withholding is allowed. Withholding quietly is not.
props.text: Redacting a colleague’s name out of an e-mail is an exemption like any other: name the ground, say what you took out, and be ready to explain it. A request can be fulfilled and still have withholdings against it — record them here rather than only in a refusal.

props.emptyText: Nothing withheld — which is also worth being able to say.

props.name: what_withheld
props.label: What was withheld
props.placeholder: Third-party names in the complaint thread

props.name: notes
props.label: Why this ground applies here
props.placeholder: The reasoning you would give a supervisory authority.

props.title: Only lawful if you tell them, in time
props.text: Art. 12(3) allows two further months where the request is complex or you have several from the same person — but only if the requester is informed within the first month, with the reasons. The date below is the date you told them; the due date moves by two months.

props.name: reason
props.label: Reason given to the requester
props.placeholder: Complexity, volume, several requests from the same person…

props.title: A refusal is an answer, and it has a deadline too
props.text: You must tell the requester without delay and at the latest within the month why you are not acting, and that they may complain to a supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy (Art. 12(4)). Recording the refusal here also files it under What we withheld, so the reasoning survives the person who wrote it.

props.name: explanation
props.label: What the requester is being told
props.placeholder: In the words they will actually read, including their right to complain.

screens.name: Search log
screens.description: Every system searched, for every request.

props.title: Search log
props.subtitle: The part organisations fail, and the part that proves they did not.

props.label: Searched nothing found
props.caption: a nil result is still evidence

props.label: Automated
props.caption: written by the knowledge base search

screens.name: Report
screens.description: Volumes, outcomes and how often the deadline was met.

props.title: Report
props.subtitle: Accountability (Art. 5(2)) is a thing you can show, or it is not a thing.

screens.name: Setup
screens.description: Request types, statuses and exemption grounds.

props.title: Setup
props.subtitle: The vocabulary this register is kept in. Data, not code.

props.title: One thing to know
props.text: Types, statuses and grounds are stored as keys, so adding a row here is enough for the register, the filters, the reports and the case file to use it. The dropdowns on the forms and the filter bar are fixed lists, so a value you add here is stored and reported on correctly but will not appear in those dropdowns until an editor adds it in App Studio.

props.emptyText: No exemption grounds configured — a refusal would have nothing to cite.

steps.message: Logged. The month runs from the date you entered — verify identity before anything is disclosed.

then.message: Identity verified. You may now disclose.

else.message: Recorded. Do not disclose — ask for what you still need, or refuse under Art. 12(6).

then.message: Add the identifiers to search on first — an account name, a customer number, an old address.

else.message: Logged. Read what came back and record what you actually found — the machine looked, you decide.

then.message: Recorded. Close the request as fulfilled once everything asked for has gone out.

else.message: Identity has not been verified — record the check on the Identity tab before disclosing anything.

steps.message: Extended by two months. Make sure the reason has actually reached the requester.

what_withheld.value: The request was refused in full.

steps.message: Refusal recorded. Tell the requester the ground, and that they may complain to a supervisory authority (Art. 12(4)).

else.message: Not while identity is unverified. Verify, or refuse under Art. 12(6) and record the ground.
